14.name: judge signs interim custody order
14.description: The judge signs an interim order keeping Mrs. Hatcher's children where they are.
evidence: By the time the judge signed the interim order keeping Mrs. Hatcher's children where they were

14.name: courtroom empties after ruling
14.description: After the ruling, the courtroom empties around Asha, leaving her alone with the aftermath.
evidence: the courtroom had emptied around Asha
in the way rooms do when the worst has not happened

14.name: Mrs. Hatcher silently thanks Asha
14.description: Mrs. Hatcher briefly touches Asha's wrist and leaves without asking the questions Asha expected.
evidence: Mrs. Hatcher pressed her hand once on the back of Asha's wrist at the door and left without asking any of the questions Asha had spent the morning bracing to deflect

14.name: caseworker contradiction remains on record
14.description: The caseworker's contradiction stays on the record after opposing counsel seizes on it.
evidence: the caseworker's contradiction sat on the record where opposing counsel had picked it up exactly as Asha had let her

14.name: Asha receives urgent messages
14.description: Asha notices her phone has been buzzing and finds missed calls, a voicemail, and a text from Claire about Marcus not coming home.
evidence: Asha stood on the courthouse steps for a long minute with the folder under her arm before she registered that her phone had been buzzing against her hip the whole time
Three missed calls from a 609 number, one voicemail, and a text from Claire that read only please call me when you can, it's about Marcus, he didn't come home last night.

14.name: Asha feels a new problem settle in
14.description: Asha realizes Marcus's disappearance is a problem no legal filing or client meeting can solve for her.
evidence: Asha put her hand flat against the stone railing and felt, for the first time since Friday, the particular cold of a problem that no filing, no disclosure, and no client in a chair across from her was going to organize for her.

14.name: Asha delays responding to Claire
14.description: Asha rereads Claire's text, pockets her phone, and decides not to listen to the voicemail yet.
evidence: Asha read the text twice on the courthouse steps and then put the phone in her coat pocket without dialing the voicemail.
The 609 number could keep until she was sitting down somewhere, and Claire's sentence had already done the work a voicemail would only repeat.

14.name: Asha walks to the parking lot
14.description: Asha leaves the courthouse steps and heads the two blocks to the lot with her folder still under her arm.
evidence: She walked the two blocks to the lot with the folder still under her arm
14.location_hint: from courthouse steps to the lot

14.name: decides to drive to Cherry Hill
14.description: Asha leaves on foot with a folder and, before fully voicing the decision to herself, chooses to drive to Cherry Hill instead of returning to the office.
evidence: She walked the two blocks to the lot with the folder still under her arm, set it on the passenger seat next to her bag, and pulled the keys out before she had decided in any sentence she could have said aloud that she was driving to Cherry Hill instead of back to the office.

14.name: drives across the bridge
14.description: Asha drives onto the bridge toward New Jersey, ignoring unanswered calls as she crosses the river.
evidence: The wipers cleared a thin grit from the windshield; she took the ramp for the bridge and let the unanswered calls sit in her pocket the whole way across the river.

14.name: ignores phone calls
14.description: Her phone buzzes, but Asha refuses to answer and decides the caller can wait or go unheard.
evidence: Her phone buzzed twice against her hip near the Haddonfield exit and she did not reach for it; whoever was calling could be returned from a curb in Cherry Hill, or not at all

14.name: rehearses Claire's address

evidence: She watched the exit signs instead, reading Claire's address back to herself from memory the way she read case captions

14.name: loses track of work and rent

evidence: noticed somewhere past the Cherry Hill Mall that she had been driving for almost an hour without thinking once about the Hatcher file or the rent due Friday

14.name: enters quiet neighborhood streets
14.description: Asha reaches the numbered streets in Cherry Hill, where the houses are quiet and set back behind leafless hedges, and she slows down at each cross street.

14.name: drives through numbered streets
14.description: Asha continues along the numbered streets, finding them quieter than she expected as she searches for the address.
evidence: The numbered streets when they came were quieter than she had expected, low brick houses set back behind hedges that had already lost their leaves, and she slowed at each cross street to check the painted curb numbers without putting the phone in her hand.

14.name: locates the correct house
14.description: After passing it twice, Asha identifies the matching house number on a low brick two-story home.
evidence: The house number matched on the third pass: a low brick two-story set behind a hedge that had gone to sticks, with a child's chalk drawing half-rained off the front walk.

14.name: parks and reviews text
14.description: Asha pulls to the curb, shuts off the engine, and rereads Claire's text while comparing it to the house number.
evidence: Asha pulled to the curb under a sycamore that had dropped most of its leaves onto the hood of a sedan in the driveway, killed the engine, and held the phone up against the steering wheel to read Claire's text again against the painted numbers on the porch column.

14.name: ignores voicemail and decides to proceed
14.description: Asha chooses not to listen to the voicemail, mentally framing it as part of an earlier version of her day and moving past indecision.
evidence: She did not play the voicemail; whatever the 609 number had wanted from her an hour ago belonged to a version of the afternoon in which she was still deciding, and she had stopped deciding somewhere on the bridge.

14.name: observes occupied house

14.name: leaves belongings in car
14.description: Asha pockets her keys, leaves the folder behind on the passenger seat, and pauses before getting out.
evidence: She put the keys in her coat pocket, left the folder on the passenger seat, and made herself sit for another count of ten before she reached for the door handle.

14.name: gets out of car

evidence: Asha pushed the door open and stepped out into air that smelled of wet leaves and someone's gas furnace kicking on a few houses down.
She did not check her phone; she dropped it into her coat pocket alongside the keys and crossed in front of the sedan

14.name: approaches the house

She went up the two concrete steps to the porch and stopped at the door

Asha knocked three times, evenly spaced

She kept her face the way she kept it in the elevator at the firm, mouth neither set nor soft, and pressed her palm flat against the side of her coat to stop herself from checking the phone in the pocket

14.name: notices the chalk drawing beneath her feet

evidence: The chalk drawing was directly under her feet now, the small circled figure half-erased by rain

14.name: fixes attention on the porch light

evidence: she made herself look at the porch light

14.name: resists checking phone

The chain slid back and the door opened onto a narrow entry

14.name: catalogues household clues

14.name: Asha notices signs of hurried departure

She was cataloguing the backpack against the baseboard

A box of cereal sat open on the counter beside two rinsed bowls; a child's drawing was anchored under a coffee mug ringed brown at the lip; the back door was closed and the deadbolt thrown.

14.name: Asha finds Claire waiting silently
14.description: Asha sees Claire standing by the table in a guarded silence that gives Asha the choice to ask easy questions or none at all.
evidence: Claire stood near the table with her hand resting on the back of a chair, not pulling it out, not looking up, and Asha understood she was being given the chance to ask the easier questions first or none at all.

14.name: asks about missing keys

14.name: Claire hesitates before answering
14.description: Claire tightens her grip on the chair and pauses without answering, showing she is struggling to respond.

14.name: Asha senses the night ahead

14.name: Asha joins Claire at the table

evidence: "let the silence do what questions could not"

14.name: Asha observes the household clues
14.description: Asha silently takes in the cereal box, rinsed bowls, and locked back door as signs of the tense situation in the house.
evidence: "The cereal box on the counter, the two rinsed bowls, the deadbolt thrown against a back door no one had come through"

14.name: Asha waits for Claire to speak

evidence: "she waited for Claire to decide what the next sentence in this house was going to be."

14.name: Asha closes the distance without touching

evidence: "Asha let her hand drift a fraction closer to Claire's on the wood, not touching, only narrowing the gap until Claire could feel the warmth of it without having to acknowledge it."

14.name: Asha silently observes the kitchen
14.description: Asha stays quiet and takes in the tense kitchen details without trying to interpret them yet.
evidence: She did not speak, and she did not lift her eyes from the small white crescent Claire's thumb had pressed into the chair's edge.

The kitchen held its small evidence around them—the open cereal box, the two rinsed bowls set side by side, the deadbolt thrown on a door no one had come through—and Asha let those things stay in the room without trying to arrange them into a story yet.

14.name: Asha waits for Claire to speak
14.description: Asha recognizes that Claire must be the one to continue the conversation and treats waiting as an active task.
evidence: Asha understood that the next sentence in the house would be hers to give and that waiting for it was now the work.

14.name: Asha reassures Claire with touch
14.description: Asha moves closer and lightly touches Claire's hand in a way that allows her to pull away if she wants.
evidence: Asha let the last inch close and set two fingertips against the side of Claire's hand, light enough that Claire could pull away if she wanted and steady enough that she would feel it if she did not.

14.name: Asha asks where Marcus is
14.description: Asha quietly asks Claire where Marcus is, pressing the issue directly.
evidence: "Where is Marcus," she said, almost under her breath

14.name: Claire avoids answering
14.description: Claire does not answer Asha's question and reacts with visible tension instead.
evidence: Claire did not answer; her shoulders drew up by a fraction and her eyes went to the back door for half a second and away again.

14.name: Asha receives Rosa's warning text
14.description: Asha's phone buzzes with a message from Rosa telling her to look at the shoes.
evidence: Asha's phone buzzed once against her hip and she glanced down out of habit—Rosa, three words, *Look at the shoes*

14.name: Asha notices men's boots by the back door

evidence: her gaze went past Claire to the mat by the back door, where a pair of men's work boots stood neatly side by side, laces tucked in, as if someone had taken them off to stay rather than to leave.

14.name: Asha withholds her response
14.description: Asha keeps her hand on Claire and stops herself from speaking further, holding back whatever she has realized.
evidence: She kept her fingertips where they were and did not say wh

14.name: Asha realizes someone stayed overnight

She kept her fingertips where they were and did not say what she had just understood

14.name: Asha withdraws from Claire and inspects the boots

and crossed the linoleum to the mat by the back door

14.name: Asha confirms the boots were recently removed

evidence: Up close the boots told her what the angle from the table had only suggested: laces tucked, not loosened; tongues upright; a fine pale grit along the welt that had dried in place rather than been tracked anywhere into the kitchen
she crouched and turned one boot a quarter inch with two fingers, enough to see the heel was set flush

14.name: Rosa warns Asha to check the mudroom closet

14.name: Claire silently watches Asha investigate

evidence: Behind her Claire had not moved
she understood that Claire was watching her watch the boots and waiting to see whether Asha would open the closet door or come back to the table first

14.name: Rosa orders Asha to open the closet immediately

evidence: Asha's phone buzzed a second time against her hip
Rosa's words land harder than the last set: *Open the closet. Now.*

14.name: receives urgent closet order

evidence: her phone buzzed a second time against her hip, and when she tipped it just enough to read the screen she saw Rosa's words land harder than the last set: *Open the closet. Now.*

14.name: approaches mudroom closet

evidence: She slid the phone back into her pocket and stood, knees stiff from the crouch, and walked the four steps to the mudroom door without turning to see what Claire's face was doing behind her.

14.name: opens closet door

evidence: The handle was cold brass, loose in its plate, and she turned it slowly
The door swung wide on a slow hinge

14.name: Claire reacts in fear
14.description: Claire makes a strained, wordless sound that suggests she has been waiting for someone else to discover what is hidden.
evidence: Behind her Claire made a sound that was not quite a word, something caught between the back of the throat and the teeth
Asha understood before the door was fully open that whatever was inside the closet was the thing Claire had been sitting at the kitchen table waiting for someone else to find.

14.name: finds Marcus's gear in closet

evidence: Inside, a coat she did not recognize hung from the middle hook, the canvas barn jacket Marcus had worn the day she met him by phone three days ago, sleeves crossed at the cuffs as if someone had folded it before hanging it up.
Below it the gear lined up in a way that read wrong by its very completeness—lunch pail, hard hat, the orange high-visibility vest she had heard him mention on the call, none of it gone with him

14.name: Asha inspects Marcus's untouched belongings
14.description: Asha examines the closet and notices Marcus left behind his work gear and wallet, suggesting he departed without taking anything.

his wallet sat flat against the wood
the orderly stillness of a man who had taken nothing with him

14.name: Asha searches for signs of foul play

evidence: She crouched and looked for the things she did not want to find, a stain, a torn sleeve, a gap in the row of work boots
and found none of it

14.name: Claire silently reacts to the discovery

the question she had come here to answer was not which of the three things Marcus had done but how long Claire had been sitting at that table waiting for someone else to look at this closet and say it out loud

14.name: Asha opens Marcus's wallet

14.name: woman closes and replaces object carefully
